**International Copper Study Group Environmental and Economic Committee Twenty Seventh Regular Meeting 6 October 2009, 10:45 a.m. – 1.00 p.m. Lisbon, Portugal** 

**ICSG/EEC27/1 (Rev.1)** 

# **Environmental and Economic Committee Provisional Agenda** 

# **1. Opening of the Meeting** 

# **2. Approval of the Agenda** 

# **3. Workshop on Policy and Incentives for Copper Scrap Trade, Recycling and Use** 

- i. Incentives for Copper Scrap Trade, Recycling and Use in Germany: Mr Stefan-Georg Fuchs, Head of Electronic Scrap Procurement, Aurubis AG 

- ii. Copper scrap trade: Mr Michael Widmer, Metals Strategist, BofA/Merrill Lynch iii. Other possible member country presentations 

This Workshop was included as a specific element of the original Copper Scrap Project proposal that was approved by member countries in October 2007. Delegates and speakers will be invited to take part in a roundtable discussion after the presentations. 

(Background Document: ICSG/EEC27/2) 

# **4. Copper Scrap Project** 

The ICSG Head of Economics and Environment will present recent ICSG Secretariat research, ongoing and finished external work, and advances in the draft final report of the Copper Scrap Project. External work advances include the Japan Copper Scrap Market Report (MERIJ), the Chinese Smelters and Semis Scrap Use Survey (BGRIMM), the report on Domestic Copper Scrap Generation in China (BGRIMM), and the report on Copper Semis Scrap Use in the Rest of the World (NATHAN Inc.). Member countries will also be invited to consider two new proposals to produce further information on the secondary copper market. 

(Background Document: ICSG/EEC27/3) 

# **5. Proposal on Copper End Use Data Agreement with ICA** 

The Secretary-General will present to member countries a proposal for a project in cooperation with the International Copper Association (ICA) on the collection, analysis and dissemination of copper end use data. 

Member countries will be invited to consider and discuss the project, seek clarification of any issues that might be unclear, and if there is consensus give approval for the project to proceed (subject to the negotiation by the secretariat of appropriate contractual arrangements with ICA). 

(Background Document: ICSG/EEC27/4) 

# **6. Leading Indicators of Copper Use: Project Proposal** 

ICSG Economist Joe Pickard will present member countries with recent research findings and a proposal for a new project on leading indicators of copper use. 

(Background Document: ICSG/EEC27/5) 

# **7. Copper Supply Constraints Coming on Stream: Impact of Tax and Investment Regimes and Final report** 

The ICSG Head of Economics and Environment will present the report on Impact of Tax and Investment Regimes on Copper Supply that has been prepared for ICSG by Mr James Otto, Mineral Economist. A summary of the final report of the project - Copper Supply Constraints Coming on Stream – will be presented, and member countries will be invited to suggest any addition

al research related to this topic. 

(Background Document: ICSG/EEC27/6) 

# **8. Review of Current and Future EEC Work Program and Priorities** 

The secretariat will provide a report on progress in relation to the approved Work Program activities and projects, including the update of China copper and alloys semis production capacity database, the recently-expanded ICSG contacts database, 2009 report on regulations affecting copper use, reuse and trade, the UN Commission on Sustainable Development review of mining, and an update on Common Fund for Commodities’ projects. Delegates will be invited to discuss progress in the Work Program and may wish to suggest additional topics. 

(Background Document ICSG/EEC27/7 and ICSG/EEC27/8) 

# **9. Other Business**
